title: An Internet for the KV Cache: Rethinking Classical Infrastructure Boundaries in the LLM Inference Age
event_hint: Vision paper proposing global-scale KV Cache content distribution system
problem: Model-side KV Cache optimizations and system-side transfer/storage optimizations evolve independently within legacy cloud boundaries, preventing optimal placement of compute and KV Cache storage across clouds and datacenters
mechanism: Proposes 'Internet for the KV Cache' vision where KV Cache management works as content-distribution system with global control plane (directory service, placement planner, prefetch scheduler) enabling store-anywhere-use-everything with bandwidth-aware movement and reuse-horizon-based tiering (hot/warm/cold)

evidence.claim: Transferring 1 GB KV Cache over fully utilized 10-Gbps link is ~19x faster and ~5.2x cheaper than AWS 8xB200 GPU cluster compute
evidence.condition: 1 GB KV Cache transfer over fully utilized 10-Gbps link

evidence.claim: Storage-compute locality is core restriction in cloud pricing due to egress costs dominating bulk data movement
evidence.condition: Wide-area cloud movement is slow and egress prices dominate cost

evidence.claim: KV Cache reuse horizons span seconds to hours in agentic workflows, enabling temporal slack for storage-compute tradeoffs
evidence.condition: Agentic workflows with multi-step reasoning, tool calls, code execution

evidence.claim: Placement governed by jointly considering reuse rates, deadlines, bandwidth, transfer and recomputation costs
evidence.condition: Model metrics (prefill FLOPs, KV size), infrastructure metrics (GPU/storage cost, bandwidth), application metrics (reuse frequency, turns)
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 1, Abstract and PDF Page 2, Introduction section

evidence.claim: Paper positions as 'call for arms' rather than implemented system
evidence.condition: Vision paper without concrete implementation or evaluation

evaluation_context: Vision paper without empirical evaluation. Quantitative examples drawn from public cloud pricing documents and prior work. Proposes three-tier storage model (hot near GPU, warm intermediate, cold distant) driven by reuse horizons. References existing systems: SkyPilot, SkyServe for inter-cloud compute; Mooncake for disaggregated KV Cache; various cache compression/eviction techniques.
limitations: Vision paper without implemented system or end-to-end evaluation. Transfer cost comparison assumes fully utilized 10-Gbps link; real-world WAN conditions with congestion, variable latency not modeled. No quantitative assessment of control plane overhead, consistency mechanisms, or failure handling. Does not address multi-tenant security or cache poisoning risks.
project_relevance: Directly addresses TPN project questions on whether network can感知 KV Cache placement and whether network-side optimization adds value beyond GPU memory scheduling. Vision proposes network as active distribution channel where bandwidth/latency/pricing directly determine KV Cache management. However, lacks concrete TTFT/TPOT measurements or comparison to state-aware network scheduling. No implementation to validate whether proposed global control plane actually improves token throughput or P95 latency versus current cloud-local approaches.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the quantitative TTFT, TPOT, or P95 latency improvements from implementing the proposed Internet for KV Cache versus current cloud-local approaches?
What are the control plane overheads for KV Cache directory lookup, placement planning, and prefetch scheduling in real-time inference workloads?
How does the proposed system handle consistency, eviction, and multi-tenant isolation across regions and clouds?
